study.question: Does moving task differentiation before history compression, and allowing feedback to affect selection rather than only values, improve click prediction under joint four-task training?
study.hypothesis: Observed baseline code uses one target/item-only local activation score and one pooled vector for all tasks; historical actions enter values but not scores. Validation click AUC is 0.6555440824200336, with only 0.5758203046092278 on empty histories. This establishes a structural constraint and scope limitation, not negative transfer. A shared nonlinear target/event scorer with task-specific output rows can select different evidence for each prediction objective. Supplying historical action embeddings to this scorer may allow task-dependent feedback selection while preserving shared feature learning. Predicted benefit is concentrated in nonempty histories; the interaction of task selection and feedback scoring is the focal mechanism, and all claims remain prospective.

nearest_work.difference: Primary archived text lines 75-85 explains target-conditioned local activation. Retain this primitive and baseline field/head adaptation; add feedback to its score input and task-indexed scoring before pooling. Not an exact DIN reproduction or a novel attention primitive.

Read pinned source lines 123-272: initializes task-specific sequence hubs with action masks and iterates aggregation/broadcast among categorical, sequence and task tokens. Here use a single shared local scorer with task-indexed output rows over the full valid history, without action-partitioned hubs, repeated broadcasts or transformer tokens.

Original version 1 abstract, introduction and preprocessing inspected via web; task-aware interaction and task/shared proxy representations are existing ideas. This study is a narrower local-selection contrast, not a priority claim or reproduction. Cached paper:infnet detailed text was unavailable; the authorized primary URL provided the text. Version 2 has a changed title; do not silently replace the pinned version 1 description.

Historical item fields and feedback embeddings as values

study.proposed_difference: Implement a four-output shared local-activation network. Each task pools the same authorized history values using its own score channel. The shared-routing control averages the channels and broadcasts that score to all four heads. Cross routing with historical action present/zeroed at the score input; action remains present in values in every cell. Score-input width and total parameters are identical across cells. Initialize all four output rows identically so task/shared scores initially coincide at a fixed feedback setting. Zero padded keys/actions/interactions before Dice statistics and scores after scoring in every cell. Relative to baseline this mask handling and nominal parameter increase are additional changes; comparisons among the four cells isolate the intended factors.
predictions: Focal contrast: task_feedback_retrieval has higher full-population click validation AUC than shared_feedback_retrieval under matched data passes.

A positive factorial interaction [(task_feedback - shared_feedback) - (task_item - shared_item)] in click AUC supports feedback-dependent task selection; task routing may help without interaction, which supports only the narrower routing hypothesis.

Secondary checks report all four task AUC/Logloss, click Logloss, auxiliary-only mean AUC, and the registered history-length slices with sample/positive/negative counts. No assumption that rare auxiliary tasks improve.

At common weights, switching routing must have no effect on zero-history pooling; any across-training empty-history score differences arise through learned shared embeddings/towers rather than history retrieval.

Added score parameters are 1123 over baseline at default widths with one 16-dimensional action field: 1024 extra input weights plus 99 extra output weights/biases. Expected total 32060552 and dense 267336, conditional on the supplied baseline counts and unchanged field specs. Host counts supersede this symbolic calculation.
falsifiers: Task routing does not improve click AUC over matched shared routing on repeated paired seeds, or worsens click Logloss materially: reject a supported click benefit from task differentiation in this implementation.
Shared feedback-aware selection matches task feedback-aware selection: feedback conditioning, rather than task conditioning, explains any baseline improvement.
No positive interaction across repeated seeds falsifies the specific claim that feedback-aware scoring especially enables task selection, even if a main effect survives.
Benefits only against baseline, with no benefit within the factorial, do not support the proposed task/feedback mechanism.

Padding-ID perturbations, target-action changes, or invalid-history changes alter eval predictions; any nonfinite forward/backward or empty-history failure blocks scientific interpretation and requires a cost-accounted repair.
alternative_explanations: Additional effective scoring rank is inseparable from allowing different task selections; nominally equal parameters do not equalize usable function capacity. The shared affine readout collapses to one function, and some action-input weights are inactive in the no-feedback cells. Do not call these effective-capacity-matched controls.

Shared dense trunk and embeddings still receive all four task gradients. Better scores alone cannot demonstrate gradient-conflict reduction or positive transfer; a later gradient-routing or single-task contrast is necessary for that claim.
Different task score gradients may regularize or optimize the shared trunk differently without semantically distinct history selection.
Feedback fields may exploit the inherited official_offline delayed-feedback availability; no production point-in-time benefit is established.
Single-seed fluctuations, prevalence and history-composition differences, unnormalized score scale, and masking-related changes relative to DIN can explain apparent gains.
The auxiliary labels concern user/category/brand actions within 24 hours, not advertisement-specific conversion attribution.

Reserve approximately 9626.9s (eight capped runs) for two additional paired seeds of all four cells if initial effects warrant. Same nominal dimensions do not assert equal measured compute.

cost_plan.stop_rule: No training, installations or agents in coding jail. Host must pass finite forward/backward and masking checks before training. Stop each job at its frozen cap and campaign work at the immutable deadline. Keep failed costs. If no robust focal or narrower main effect survives paired comparisons, record a null/negative result and choose the strongest supported existing reference rather than declare success. Do not use held-out outcomes to adapt this study.

knowledge_assessments.rationale: The local code confirms a shared history bottleneck; task-aware sequence aggregation is a relevant precedent. Primary version 1 and pinned implementation were inspected separately.
knowledge_assessments.transformed_mechanism: Replace one shared history score by task-indexed local activation, crossed with feedback-aware selection; omit hub aggregation, broadcasts, task history masks and proxy tokens.
knowledge_assessments.nearest_work_difference: One pooling stage with shared trunk and task score rows, rather than recurrent cross-group task/proxy token interaction. This is an adaptation study, not verified novelty.
knowledge_assessments.falsifier: Task routing has no reproducible click gain over the shared-scoring controls, or shared selection explains all gains.

knowledge_assessments.rationale: Retrieved sparse filtering acts after pooling and would add a separate intervention before the task pooling limitation is measured. No local evidence for sparse filtering was supplied.
knowledge_assessments.nearest_work_difference: Current contrasts concern task-conditioned compression before prediction rather than competitive sparse feature filtering after compression. SSR primary paper was not audited.
knowledge_assessments.falsifier: If shared pooling is adequate but downstream activation interference is observed in later diagnostics, reconsider sparse filtering with dense replacement controls.

host_checks_required: Use actual frozen FeatureMap; assert source fields and embedding widths agree with baseline; verify default parameter counts and all four outputs [B,1] finite in [0,1].
Forward and sum-four-BCE backward in training mode at a batch size greater than 1 and under host BF16; verify finite dense gradients and sparse optimizer compatibility.
In eval, change padded item/action IDs at fixed mask and valid events: predictions identical. Change current action ID: predictions identical because only historical action positions are read.
All-zero masks yield exactly zero pooled vectors and finite task predictions; mixed empty/nonempty masks, full histories, and history length 0 are shape-safe.

With identical initialized weights, task/shared routing outputs coincide for both feedback settings; after a training step confirm task score rows can diverge and shared routing always pools identical vectors for all heads.

At a common checkpoint, temporarily average task scores to measure prediction sensitivity; this is exploratory mediation evidence, not substitute training or held-out selection. Charge any validation diagnostics.
Collect parameter counts, peak GPU memory, allocated GPU seconds, examples, wall time and validation inference throughput/p50/p95 latency for every cell. Do not claim compute parity from dimensions.
